source: Built deterministically from liraasa_1_2.json (sha256 12e9d262ec56b1515dba196b2ecf7de432dae611d7a5af213dc206f477441fe3) by scripts/integrate_2_0.ts, applying the changeset 2026-10-18-lexicon-2-0 and 2026-10-18-lexicon-2-0-review (ADR-0016). This JSON is the single source of truth for Liraasa 2.0.

phonology.vowels: a e i o u (pure); adjacent vowels are separate syllables
phonology.consonants_core: l m n r s v y
phonology.consonants_other: b d p t g h z k c f j (sh, ch only in colour/number words)
phonology.new_root_template: two syllables, consonant-initial, vowel-final, letters from the inventory, no initial cluster (kr-, tr- grandfathered), no three-consonant cluster, no doubled letter, at least two edits from every active word
phonology.function_word_template: one to three syllables, vowel-final, no initial cluster; at least two edits from every active word; monosyllables may sit one edit from another monosyllable only if they belong to different syntactic positions (declared list)
protected_exceptions: 39 amor compounds (legacy canon): 20 ending -amor, 19 beginning amor-

morphology.compounding: MODIFIER+HEAD written together; head rightmost; components must be active 1.0 headwords; a compound's verb class follows its first letter

lexicalised_derivations.vanruyo: soldier; warrior (one who wages war): vanru + -yo
lexicalised_derivations.zirmeyo: mage; sorcerer; witch; magician; wizard: zirme + -yo
lexicalised_derivations.ramupago: memory palace; where memories are kept: ramu + -pago
lexicalised_derivations.lasopago: a place of silence; a retreat: laso + -pago
lexicalised_derivations.lumipago: sanctum; the holy of holies: lumi + -pago
lexicalised_derivations.lumiyo: lightbearer; one who brings light: lumi + -yo
lexicalised_derivations.devoyo: believer; one of the faithful: devo + -yo
lexicalised_derivations.kersopago: nursery; a place where young things grow: kerso + -pago
lexicalised_derivations.ranbepago: a place where one's strength returns: ranbe + -pago

derivation_defaults.-yo: one who does R; one devoted to R
derivation_defaults.-ti: a little or dear R (also affectionate)
derivation_defaults.constraints: one form OR one derivation, then -ti, then -ri (unchanged). Prefer a listed derivation when one exists.

image_compounds.name: Image compounds
image_compounds.rule: MODIFIER + HEAD, written as one word, where MODIFIER is any root in 'modifiers' and HEAD any root in 'heads'. Meaning: '<modifier adjective> <head>', that is, <head template> <modifier sense>. Example: luno + savali = lunosavali, 'moonlit kiss; an intimate kiss recalling moonlight'. Every such pair is valid Liraasa and needs no 'new' flag. Verb class follows the first letter, as for all compounds.
image_compounds.why: 394 dictionary entries followed this exact pattern. Listing them added size but no expressive power, and implied that unlisted pairs (moonlit voice, rain-washed promise) were less valid. As a pattern, all 57 x 31 = 1,767 pairs are available.

scope_operators.rule: immediately before the constituent they scope over (noun phrase, verb, adjective, number, clause-introducer such as si)

stacking.scope: left scopes over right (G1); ne negates everything to its right up to the verb

rulings_1_0.ruling: Every preverbal operator scopes over everything to its right. Pre-constituent operators (ne, doli, tu, yesta, pendi, vinto) scope over the single constituent that follows them.
si means only 'if'. 'whether' is ki-oro. 0.8 texts that used si for 'whether' are read under 0.8 rules.
povi = ability; nosi = epistemic possibility (might); dagi = permission (may, be allowed). 0.8's double use of nosi is split.
'must (logically)' = inferential evidential tosu + seye; musi is only obligation or circumstantial necessity.
Intent is the verb chain 'dorvada sidu VERB' (intend to); kopi is only 'hope to'. Deliberately = la dorvasan; accidentally = la dorvanasan.
noma marks a clause as contrary to fact. 'should have' = po noma suvi; 'could have' = po noma povi; 'would have' = po viki (in a consequence clause) or po noma viki.
fututi in the approach slot means 'about to': Maivo po fututi pagopa = I was about to leave. As a clause-initial time word it still means 'soon'.
loki covers both 'still' and 'keep on'; no separate continuative is added.
Before a number or quantity, lusu = at least, mosa = at most, gase = approximately; pendi = exactly.
oro A oro B = either A or B; ne A ne B = neither A nor B; doli si = only if; yesta si = even if; 'si …, ata doli si …' = if and only if.
nevi + noun phrase = despite: nevi li zeldo, despite the resistance. nevi + clause = although.
vobi + noun phrase = for the benefit of / on behalf of (unchanged), and combines with any operator.
ata is 'and' only; additive 'also' is tu.

vaku (make), lesvu (let) and tekvu (prevent) fill the verb slot of the main clause; the actor follows, then the actor's own [ne] [phase] [effort] verb. Tense, modal and evidential belong to the main clause only.
ne before an operator negates the operator; ne after it negates the event: po ne vazdi lirala = didn't manage to sing; po vazdi ne lirala = managed not to sing.

At most one word per slot. hiro/teki do not combine with roni or tefa. tavki excludes fututi (same slot). The effort slot (telvo, vazdi, fesmo) excludes tefa. noma requires a tense, modal or si-clause context.
la nerponasan = unexpectedly; kroti ola = previously; nayo ola = meanwhile/simultaneously; krotiapo = subsequently. No new words.
A hozi-topic opens the clause; vinto may then mark a focus inside it. hozi and vinto never mark the same constituent.
Texts dated before 1.0 are interpreted with the 0.8 lexicon and rules. A 1.0 reader meeting a retired spelling looks it up in legacy.retired and reads the 1.0 replacement.
tisebitivu (sword), tibivu (rope), kaldopago (prison) and zeldoyo (rebel) are fixed meanings of regular derivations.

A raho-clause that does not end the sentence is closed by a comma in writing and a pause in speech: Li sabeyo raho vismava eli, ne yehu vimova li vordu. (Found in stress-testing: without the pause the main verb is read inside the relative clause.)
seye, mufe, poye, pifu and zoke never open a clause. 'Perhaps, …' at the start of a sentence is written with the clause-final poye. (Found in stress-testing.)
venreva (come) with an event as subject means 'take place, happen': Li dapadonu po venreva kroti li nilvu, the sale took place before winter.

rulings_0_8_carried.ruling: The JSON is authoritative; the workbook is generated. Language field and files are named Liraasa.
An unused form may receive a gloss only when its compositional meaning is predictable, approved case by case, and recorded in authorized_changes.
Frozen for 0.8. No canonical root is respelled; the 40-root queue carries forward unchanged.

A standalone tense particle opening a paragraph or turn (Po — / Futu —) sets a frame: following unmarked main clauses take that tense until another tense particle, pressa, or the end of the paragraph. Optional. Time words do not set a frame, so 0.7 texts keep their meaning.
li may be omitted in everyday speech as well as verse when the referent is obvious; never when ambiguous. baba may be omitted only in verse.
sige clauses never inherit tense; they are always marked. Tense inheritance applies to fime, raho, kube, nayo, kasa, kopisa and tuni.
deyaapo is kept as a fossil (it retains the retired past marker apo). apo is not used in new compounds; say vesno de deyaapo.
amorliraa, amorrinbaa and amorvulraa are correct; each a is its own syllable.
A certainty marker (or zoke) precedes ki: Taivo lirala poye ki?
Registers are defined in the grammar guide. The lexicon keeps everyday and poetic labels; sacred is added only to headwords whose root meaning is inherently sacred, after review.
New vocabulary is sized by genuine gaps, not by the 120-150 target.
The diminutive -ti may attach to personal names as an affectionate or teasing form (Dorinti).

eli/ola (and eliri/olari) stand alone for things, situations and discourse (ola = what was just said; eli = what follows). For people use eli-nela/ola-nela or saivo, except presentational Eli ka NAME.

ne precedes what it negates: verb or modal (after tense), copula (ne ka), noun phrase or fragment (Ne eli), or a contrasted constituent (ne X, nara Y). Negation is compositional: ne + nuna- is a positive (avoid).

Everyday speech may omit a repeated subject in coordinated clauses and in answers, omit a repeated predicate after a contrasting subject (Dorin, ne.), answer with tense + verb (Po sapusia.), and echo a word with ki. Speech may break off after any particle; the listener may complete it.

ki may close the main clause before an appended direct quotation (Taivo vurlova ki, fime maivo senosia: "...") as well as after it (0.7 order). Embedded wh-questions keep the wh-word in place with no ki; embedded yes/no questions use si (whether).
Inside an inheriting clause: tefa marks prior action, nayo/roni simultaneous, futu subsequent (future-in-past), sahi habitual.

The root (form 1) is the noun of action or thing (juba, donu, tali). A verb phrase becomes a noun phrase with sidu (Sidu lisrola ka livna de taivo) or a clause with fime (Fime taivo po relnura ka baba juba).
[toda|rada|muya|poka|somi|nuna] [li|eli|ola|OWNER de] [NUMBER] [ADJ...] NOUN[-ti][-ri] [de ...] [raho ...]. toda N = every N; toda li N = all the N; toda OWNER de N = all OWNER's N.
X ka sambasan ko Y (same as); X ka sambanasan da Y (different from); gase NP alone = like NP (simile); gase ADJ gase NP = as ADJ as NP. Lotero silda, ... = on the other hand.

rulings_1_2.ruling: A time word or time correlative (eli-krono, deyapressa, fututi, ki-krono's answers…) may open its clause or close it. When it opens the clause, the comma after it is optional. Only the four frame words zafra, finra, lanto and kenvi are opening-only, and they keep their comma.

A single oro joins two equal constituents, exactly as ata does: miru oro nami, water or food. It may also open a clause or line that continues the one before ("Or …"). The pair oro A oro B is the emphatic "either A or B".
examples: oro maivo ke li suma ki?

rulings_1_2.topic: Give-type verbs: where the recipient goes
rulings_1_2.ruling: A verb of giving (give, lend, send, owe, sell, pay, bring, teach, show) takes VERB THEME ala RECIPIENT. When the recipient is a pronoun it may instead stand bare straight after the verb: VERB PRONOUN THEME. Any other recipient takes ala.
examples: Fisa, rimara tressa cono ala maivo.

rulings_1_2.topic: Which side of de is the owner
rulings_1_2.ruling: In X de Y the owner is Y, read as English "X of Y": li bumre de li cilni, the bread of the city; li lira de amor, the song of love. One exception: a pronoun or a personal name (pilo, father, used as a name included) standing before de is the owner, read as English "X's Y": maivo de lira, my song; pilo de bumre, father's bread. A pronoun is the owner wherever it stands: li purma de maivo, my parent. Fractions (tressa de cuara) are their own construction.
examples: Li bitiri de pilo ka su li tabu.
Father's tools are on the table.
Eli bumre ka sambasan ko pilo de bumre.
This bread is the same as father's bread.

rulings_1_2.ruling: After a number or a quantifier the plural -ri is optional: the number already says how many. Choose by sound and meter. Without a number or quantifier, a plural noun takes -ri.
examples: Maivo po vimova muya jemlari en li folni.
I saw many insects on the flower.

rulings_1_2.topic: An adjective standing as a noun
rulings_1_2.ruling: An adjective may stand as a noun phrase on its own only after an article or determiner (li, eli, ola, baba): li ramumomvisan, the forgotten. Without one, an adjective needs its noun.
examples: yesta li raleri de li sadori de li ramumomvisan po lenila maivori de lira.
even the echoes of the sorrows of the forgotten heard our song

rulings_1_2.ruling: Liraasa has no word for "about / concerning". A song, story or word about something is a de phrase under G27: li lira de amor, the song of (about) love. After a verb of saying, give the verb an object rather than su: po sarbisia lirari de amor, wrote songs of love.
examples: Li ralelirapatu de li lira ka melosan.
Li veluri po sarbisia lirari de amor.
The stars wrote songs of love.

rulings_1_2.ruling: A command has no subject: the clause opens at the verb (slot 3 notes), softened with fisa. A person addressed is a noun phrase set off by commas, at the start or end of the clause. In verse, once the time has been set, the bare present may narrate past events.
examples: Taivo viki pagopa ligo maivo ki, maivo de amor?
Would you come near me, my love?

rulings_1_2.ruling: When de joins two candidates for owner, the owner is decided in this order: a pronoun, then a personal name (pilo, mare used as names included), then the default of 1.2:G27 (in X de Y, Y is the owner). Pilo de maivo is my father, not father's me. PRONOUN de PRONOUN is allowed, and the right-hand pronoun is the owner: taivo de maivo, you of mine.

yuta + noun phrase names the instrument or means of an action: with, using, by means of. It fills the ADJUNCTS slot like the other prepositions. It never means accompaniment: "with a friend" stays ko.
examples: Maivo lallela li dorbi yuta li kemye.
I open the door with the key.
Li lirayo po yugemeyiya saivo yuta melo.
The singer healed him with music.
Saivori po ka vazranasan yuta benamolu.

rulings_1_2.ruling: A quantifier joined to krono with a hyphen gives a frequency adverbial: muya-krono often, poka-krono rarely, rada-krono each time. Like the other -krono correlatives it opens or closes its clause (1.2:G24). The pattern is limited to krono; muya, poka and rada form no other correlatives.
revo-sabesia (know again: recognize) and yave-donuda (give together: share) join revo-vimova and revo-lirala as curated metaphors. The motion prefixes otherwise stay non-productive.

Kinship words are neutral: purma parent, famli sibling, linu child, purmafamli aunt or uncle. Gender is marked only when it matters, by a compound with minva (female) or tarnu (male) where the lexicon has one (minvalinu daughter, tarnufamli brother), and otherwise by the adjective before the noun (minvasan purmafamli, aunt). mare and pilo remain mother and father. Kin by marriage compound with rilde: rildemare mother-in-law. Neither gender root is the negative of the other.
examples: Li tarnufamli de taivo ka corvisan.

rulings_2_0.ruling: Declare devo / devi and nevi / devi as permitted one-edit pairs.

rulings_2_0.topic: Colour bases in compounds; compounds lexicalised with -ti
rulings_2_0.ruling: Colour bases may act as the modifier in a dictionary compound, and a compound may be lexicalised with -ti.
aurumijuba and vanajuba become dictionary headwords as well as colour words.
Image compounds: any listed modifier + any listed head is a valid word with a predictable meaning, no 'new' flag needed (see pattern_compounds).

Derivations are fully productive with default readings: R+yo = one who does R, or one devoted to R; R+vu = a big or intense R; R+pago = the place of R; R+ti = a little or dear R. They attach to any root or compound (as lemudonuyo and mambiletoyo already do). Listed derivations keep their fixed meanings and override the default.

A compound may take a compound as one of its two parts: MODIFIER + HEAD still joins exactly two headwords, either of which may itself be a compound (larbopago + safa = larbopagosafa). 1.2 avoided nesting; 2.0 allows it.

Vowels are pure, as in Spanish or Italian. l m n s v b d p t f k sound as in English; y as in "yes"; r is a single tap, as in Spanish "pero"; g is always hard, as in "go"; h as in "hope"; z as in "zone". c is always "ch" as in "chant", before every vowel: ca = cha, co = cho, and likewise ce, ci, cu. j is the voiced partner of c, as in "jewel". sh is as in "shade"; ch, written only in a few colour and number words, is the same sound as c.

Every written vowel is its own syllable (0.8:R8), but in singing neighbouring vowels may glide into one note: benaasa may be sung be-na-a-sa or be-naa-sa. The spelling never changes; the songwriter chooses the count the melody needs.
A foreign name is not translated. It is copied as closely as Liraasa letters allow, choosing among near spellings by how the name sounds and sings.

rulings_0_8.ruling: The JSON is authoritative; the workbook is generated. Language field and files are named Liraasa.
An unused form may receive a gloss only when its compositional meaning is predictable, approved case by case, and recorded in authorized_changes.
Frozen for 0.8. No canonical root is respelled; the 40-root queue carries forward unchanged.

A standalone tense particle opening a paragraph or turn (Po — / Futu —) sets a frame: following unmarked main clauses take that tense until another tense particle, pressa, or the end of the paragraph. Optional. Time words do not set a frame, so 0.7 texts keep their meaning.
li may be omitted in everyday speech as well as verse when the referent is obvious; never when ambiguous. baba may be omitted only in verse.
sige clauses never inherit tense; they are always marked. Tense inheritance applies to fime, raho, kube, nayo, kasa, kopisa and tuni.
deyaapo is kept as a fossil (it retains the retired past marker apo). apo is not used in new compounds; say vesno de deyaapo.
amorliraa, amorrinbaa and amorvulraa are correct; each a is its own syllable.
A certainty marker (or zoke) precedes ki: Taivo lirala poye ki?
Registers are defined in the grammar guide. The lexicon keeps everyday and poetic labels; sacred is added only to headwords whose root meaning is inherently sacred, after review.
New vocabulary is sized by genuine gaps, not by the 120-150 target.
The diminutive -ti may attach to personal names as an affectionate or teasing form (Dorinti).

eli/ola (and eliri/olari) stand alone for things, situations and discourse (ola = what was just said; eli = what follows). For people use eli-nela/ola-nela or saivo, except presentational Eli ka NAME.

ne precedes what it negates: verb or modal (after tense), copula (ne ka), noun phrase or fragment (Ne eli), or a contrasted constituent (ne X, nara Y). Negation is compositional: ne + nuna- is a positive (avoid).

Everyday speech may omit a repeated subject in coordinated clauses and in answers, omit a repeated predicate after a contrasting subject (Dorin, ne.), answer with tense + verb (Po sapusia.), and echo a word with ki. Speech may break off after any particle; the listener may complete it.

ki may close the main clause before an appended direct quotation (Taivo vurlova ki, fime maivo senosia: "...") as well as after it (0.7 order). Embedded wh-questions keep the wh-word in place with no ki; embedded yes/no questions use si (whether).
Inside an inheriting clause: tefa marks prior action, nayo/roni simultaneous, futu subsequent (future-in-past), sahi habitual.

The root (form 1) is the noun of action or thing (juba, donu, tali). A verb phrase becomes a noun phrase with sidu (Sidu lisrola ka livna de taivo) or a clause with fime (Fime taivo po relnura ka baba juba).
[toda|rada|muya|poka|somi|nuna] [li|eli|ola|OWNER de] [NUMBER] [ADJ...] NOUN[-ti][-ri] [de ...] [raho ...]. toda N = every N; toda li N = all the N; toda OWNER de N = all OWNER's N.
X ka sambasan ko Y (same as); X ka sambanasan da Y (different from); gase NP alone = like NP (simile); gase ADJ gase NP = as ADJ as NP. Lotero silda, ... = on the other hand.

reserved_root_bank.note: Short two-syllable roots (consonant-vowel-consonant-vowel) that still fit every rule: at least two edits from every active word in 1.2 plus this patch, and from each other. The most singable root shape is nearly full, so spend these deliberately: on frequent concepts whose words are long. Unassigned; not part of the language until you give one a meaning. Checked against every Liraasa word in the 1.2 file (headwords, forms, small words, numbers, colours, example sentences) and in this patch. Roots with c are left out because its pronunciation is not fixed in the sound section.

changesets_1_2_full.author: nicolas
changesets_1_2_full.summary: Grammar rulings G24–G31 from the open-questions review of 2026-10-17 (ADR-0012), and the three examples ADR-0011 left to revise. 1.1 stays vocabulary-only (ADR-0009); these land on top of it.

rulings.ruling: A time word or time correlative (eli-krono, deyapressa, fututi, ki-krono's answers…) may open its clause or close it. When it opens the clause, the comma after it is optional. Only the four frame words zafra, finra, lanto and kenvi are opening-only, and they keep their comma.

A single oro joins two equal constituents, exactly as ata does: miru oro nami, water or food. It may also open a clause or line that continues the one before ("Or …"). The pair oro A oro B is the emphatic "either A or B".
examples: oro maivo ke li suma ki?

rulings.topic: Give-type verbs: where the recipient goes
rulings.ruling: A verb of giving (give, lend, send, owe, sell, pay, bring, teach, show) takes VERB THEME ala RECIPIENT. When the recipient is a pronoun it may instead stand bare straight after the verb: VERB PRONOUN THEME. Any other recipient takes ala.
examples: Fisa, rimara tressa cono ala maivo.

rulings.topic: Which side of de is the owner
rulings.ruling: In X de Y the owner is Y, read as English "X of Y": li bumre de li cilni, the bread of the city; li lira de amor, the song of love. One exception: a pronoun or a personal name (pilo, father, used as a name included) standing before de is the owner, read as English "X's Y": maivo de lira, my song; pilo de bumre, father's bread. A pronoun is the owner wherever it stands: li purma de maivo, my parent. Fractions (tressa de cuara) are their own construction.
examples: Li bitiri de pilo ka su li tabu.
Father's tools are on the table.
Eli bumre ka sambasan ko pilo de bumre.
This bread is the same as father's bread.
Li bumre de li cilni ka sambanasan da eli bumre.
City bread is different from this bread.
Nullo de deyaapo, maivo po ne somusia.

rulings.ruling: After a number or a quantifier the plural -ri is optional: the number already says how many. Choose by sound and meter. Without a number or quantifier, a plural noun takes -ri.
examples: Maivo po vimova muya jemlari en li folni.
I saw many insects on the flower.

rulings.topic: An adjective standing as a noun
rulings.ruling: An adjective may stand as a noun phrase on its own only after an article or determiner (li, eli, ola, baba): li ramumomvisan, the forgotten. Without one, an adjective needs its noun.
examples: yesta li raleri de li sadori de li ramumomvisan po lenila maivori de lira.
even the echoes of the sorrows of the forgotten heard our song

rulings.ruling: Liraasa has no word for "about / concerning". A song, story or word about something is a de phrase under G27: li lira de amor, the song of (about) love. After a verb of saying, give the verb an object rather than su: po sarbisia lirari de amor, wrote songs of love.
examples: Li ralelirapatu de li lira ka melosan.
Li veluri po sarbisia lirari de amor.
The stars wrote songs of love.

rulings.ruling: A command has no subject: the clause opens at the verb (slot 3 notes), softened with fisa. A person addressed is a noun phrase set off by commas, at the start or end of the clause. In verse, once the time has been set, the bare present may narrate past events.
examples: Taivo viki pagopa ligo maivo ki, maivo de amor?
Would you come near me, my love?

ops.to: Time words open or close a clause; the opening comma is optional; zafra, finra, lanto, kenvi stay opening-only.
ops.reason: Canon closes clauses with eli-krono (Saivo po venreva pendi eli-krono; Li navutrana ne ka sovesan eli-krono) and once omits the comma (Eli-krono maivo lirala). Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: A lone oro joins two equal parts like ata, and may open a continuing clause; oro A oro B is emphatic either/or.
ops.reason: The function-word table's own example is a lone oro (miru oro nami). Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: A give-type verb takes THEME ala RECIPIENT, or a bare pronoun recipient straight after the verb.
ops.reason: Canon writes guraga maivo (pendi) (dossa) cono four times; every bare recipient in canon is a pronoun. Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: In X de Y the owner is Y, except a pronoun or personal name before de is the owner; a pronoun is always the owner.
ops.reason: Fits every one of the 65 canon de phrases, including pilo de bumre, livna de taivo and nullo de deyaapo. Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: -ri is optional after a number or quantifier.
ops.reason: Canon has both dossa veluri and dossa cono, muya jemlari and muya marna. Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: An adjective stands as a noun only after an article or determiner.
ops.reason: li ramumomvisan, "the forgotten", in Lira de Kronoasa; the -san ending keeps it parseable. Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: "About" is a de phrase; no new word.
ops.reason: 1.0 has no word for about; a de phrase is short, singable and reads as English verse (songs of love). Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: Commands have no subject (fisa softens); address is set off by commas; verse may narrate in the present.
ops.reason: Commands and address are already written this way in canon (Vulravelmava maivo de yendo, fisa; …ki, maivo de amor?); the narrative present gives verse metrical freedom. Author's ruling, 2026-10-17.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.to: Maivo de benasan melo opioa lumi.
ops.reason: ADR-0011: melo bena is noun + noun, melo sat in the verb slot, and the pronoun owner lacked de. Rewritten to keep the gloss "My good music hopes for light" using only existing forms.
ops.author: nicolas

ops.from: Lotero silda, li cilni ka lasona.
ops.to: Loterosan silda, li cilni ka lasona.
ops.reason: ADR-0011: lotero silda is noun + noun; loterosan is the adjective "other".
ops.author: nicolas

ops.from: Maivo po lemula baba lotero lermi.
ops.to: Maivo po lemula baba loterosan lermi.
ops.reason: ADR-0011: lotero lermi is noun + noun; loterosan is the adjective "other".

changesets_1_2_full.author: nicolas
changesets_1_2_full.summary: The 1.2 lexicon update (ADR-0013): rulings G32–G36, 57 primal roots, 22 compounds, 2 function words, 3 frequency correlatives, 24 lexicalised derivations, 2 curated motion metaphors, 3 reglosses, 6 predictable slots activated, and the protected-exceptions label repaired. Applied after 2026-10-17-grammar-rulings by npm run integrate:1.2.

rulings.ruling: When de joins two candidates for owner, the owner is decided in this order: a pronoun, then a personal name (pilo, mare used as names included), then the default of 1.2:G27 (in X de Y, Y is the owner). Pilo de maivo is my father, not father's me. PRONOUN de PRONOUN is allowed, and the right-hand pronoun is the owner: taivo de maivo, you of mine.

yuta + noun phrase names the instrument or means of an action: with, using, by means of. It fills the ADJUNCTS slot like the other prepositions. It never means accompaniment: "with a friend" stays ko.
examples: Maivo lallela li dorbi yuta li kemye.
I open the door with the key.
Li lirayo po yugemeyiya saivo yuta melo.
The singer healed him with music.
Saivori po ka vazranasan yuta benamolu.

rulings.ruling: A quantifier joined to krono with a hyphen gives a frequency adverbial: muya-krono often, poka-krono rarely, rada-krono each time. Like the other -krono correlatives it opens or closes its clause (1.2:G24). The pattern is limited to krono; muya, poka and rada form no other correlatives.
revo-sabesia (know again: recognize) and yave-donuda (give together: share) join revo-vimova and revo-lirala as curated metaphors. The motion prefixes otherwise stay non-productive.

Kinship words are neutral: purma parent, famli sibling, linu child, purmafamli aunt or uncle. Gender is marked only when it matters, by a compound with minva (female) or tarnu (male) where the lexicon has one (minvalinu daughter, tarnufamli brother), and otherwise by the adjective before the noun (minvasan purmafamli, aunt). mare and pilo remain mother and father. Kin by marriage compound with rilde: rildemare mother-in-law. Neither gender root is the negative of the other.
examples: Li tarnufamli de taivo ka corvisan.

changesets_2_0_full.summary: Liraasa 2.0 (ADR-0016), from the author's patch "Liraasa 2.0: the great lexicon expansion": rulings 2.0:G37–G42 (word-building only; no clause, order or inflection rule changes), 10 roots and 346 compounds, 276 slots activated, 207 glosses edited, 77 lexicalised derivations, 391 template headwords moved into the image-compound pattern.

rulings.ruling: Declare devo / devi and nevi / devi as permitted one-edit pairs.

rulings.topic: Colour bases in compounds; compounds lexicalised with -ti
rulings.ruling: Colour bases may act as the modifier in a dictionary compound, and a compound may be lexicalised with -ti.
aurumijuba and vanajuba become dictionary headwords as well as colour words.
Image compounds: any listed modifier + any listed head is a valid word with a predictable meaning, no 'new' flag needed (see pattern_compounds).

Derivations are fully productive with default readings: R+yo = one who does R, or one devoted to R; R+vu = a big or intense R; R+pago = the place of R; R+ti = a little or dear R. They attach to any root or compound (as lemudonuyo and mambiletoyo already do). Listed derivations keep their fixed meanings and override the default.

A compound may take a compound as one of its two parts: MODIFIER + HEAD still joins exactly two headwords, either of which may itself be a compound (larbopago + safa = larbopagosafa). 1.2 avoided nesting; 2.0 allows it.

image_compounds.name: Image compounds
image_compounds.rule: MODIFIER + HEAD, written as one word, where MODIFIER is any root in 'modifiers' and HEAD any root in 'heads'. Meaning: '<modifier adjective> <head>', that is, <head template> <modifier sense>. Example: luno + savali = lunosavali, 'moonlit kiss; an intimate kiss recalling moonlight'. Every such pair is valid Liraasa and needs no 'new' flag. Verb class follows the first letter, as for all compounds.
image_compounds.why: 394 dictionary entries followed this exact pattern. Listing them added size but no expressive power, and implied that unlisted pairs (moonlit voice, rain-washed promise) were less valid. As a pattern, all 57 x 31 = 1,767 pairs are available.

morphology.derivation_defaults.-yo: one who does R; one devoted to R
morphology.derivation_defaults.-ti: a little or dear R (also affectionate)
morphology.derivation_defaults.constraints: one form OR one derivation, then -ti, then -ri (unchanged). Prefer a listed derivation when one exists.

reserved_root_bank.note: Short two-syllable roots (consonant-vowel-consonant-vowel) that still fit every rule: at least two edits from every active word in 1.2 plus this patch, and from each other. The most singable root shape is nearly full, so spend these deliberately: on frequent concepts whose words are long. Unassigned; not part of the language until you give one a meaning. Checked against every Liraasa word in the 1.2 file (headwords, forms, small words, numbers, colours, example sentences) and in this patch. Roots with c are left out because its pronunciation is not fixed in the sound section.

changesets_2_0_full.summary: The 2.0 grammar-guide review (ADR-0016 addendum): rulings 2.0:G43 (consonant values), G44 (neighbouring vowels in song) and G45 (foreign names), from the author's answers of 2026-10-18; lumiasa reglossed "Divine Light, Goddess", then "Her Divine Light"; two gloss typos fixed. No grammar rule changes.

rulings.ruling: Vowels are pure, as in Spanish or Italian. l m n s v b d p t f k sound as in English; y as in "yes"; r is a single tap, as in Spanish "pero"; g is always hard, as in "go"; h as in "hope"; z as in "zone". c is always "ch" as in "chant", before every vowel: ca = cha, co = cho, and likewise ce, ci, cu. j is the voiced partner of c, as in "jewel". sh is as in "shade"; ch, written only in a few colour and number words, is the same sound as c.

Every written vowel is its own syllable (0.8:R8), but in singing neighbouring vowels may glide into one note: benaasa may be sung be-na-a-sa or be-naa-sa. The spelling never changes; the songwriter chooses the count the melody needs.
A foreign name is not translated. It is copied as closely as Liraasa letters allow, choosing among near spellings by how the name sounds and sings.
